newsitem.title: UK: Bean bags replace chairs as ad agency chases ideas.
newsitem.headline: Bean bags replace chairs as ad agency chases ideas.

text.p: A British ad agency has dispensed with traditional offices and desks and replaced them with bean bags, lockers and mobile phones in a bid to boost creative thinking.

"We call it romping and it's about talking, gathering and interacting rather than being locked away in your own little office," Ann Harris a partner in the Howell Henry Chaldecott Lury & Partners (HHCL) agency told Reuters recently.

Agency staff do not have their own desk but "hot- desk" -- using an available desk as the need arises. They are assigned a laptop computer each and a mobile phone. Personal belongings are kept in lockers.
Traditional office furniture is dispensed with.
Those in search of inspiration can perch on brightly coloured bean bags or recline on sofas. The orthodoxy of office pot plants gives way to bowls offering a plentiful supply of fresh fruit.
There are also brightly coloured areas where staff can have meetings and quiet areas for creative thought.
"We wanted to get away from that old hierarchical office culture where the bigger your office, the more important you are," said Harris.
The agency, whose clients include the soft drink Tango and the Automobile Association, has also created meeting rooms without chairs.
"If every one is standing, it means a meeting is over and done with more quickly so it saves a lot of time," she said.
Another London agency St Luke's also has an unorthodox working environment.

Its staff have their own mobile phones and use computers which are scattered around, as required. The agency boasts its own artist in residence who creates wild sculptures that are dotted around the building - a converted toffee factory.

Marketing director David Abrahams said: "We don't want an old fashioned set-up where the boss sits in the biggest office. We don't have a boss as such because the agency is a co-operative and all the members of staff own it."

The only offices the agency has are dedicated client rooms. In the Boots Co Plc room there is a full size cosmetics counter and the Midland Bank Plc room contains the famous blue Midland Bank sofa which is used in its advertising campaigns.

Even the more traditional large ad agencies are looking at new ways of working. WPP Group Plc, which owns J. Walter Thompson and Ogilvy & Mather is introducing a "Space Programme" to encourage its agency networks to use their office space more imaginatively and more effectively.
"We can improve our communications, speed of response and efficiency by improving the design and layout of the premises in which we invest almost $250 million each year, " said a spokeswoman.

Removing desks from offices means that there are cost savings to be had as more people can work in a smaller space, but HHCL's Harris said that these futuristic offices are not necessarily cheap. "Technology such as the complex phone system we had installed so that everyone can be contacted on a mobile is expensive," she said.
She added that it is not an environment that suits everybody "You need to be a pretty confident sort of person to enjoy this sort of atmosphere where you sit next to someone different every day.
'Fortunately most people in advertising are like that."
